title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 77 (Duty to register charges)

content.overview: Every company creating a charge on its property, assets or undertaking must register the prescribed particulars and creating instrument with the Registrar within thirty days. The Registrar may allow registration within sixty days of creation on additional fees; if not registered within that period, the company must seek extension under section 87. An unregistered charge is not taken into account by a liquidator or other creditor unless registered and certified, but the secured repayment obligation is not thereby erased.

content.study: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 77 (Duty to register charges). A company creating a charge within or outside India on its property, assets or any undertaking must file the prescribed particulars, signed by the company and charge-holder, together with the instrument creating the charge, with the Registrar within thirty days of creation, in the prescribed form and on payment of prescribed fees. The Registrar may, on application by the company, allow registration within sixty days of creation on payment of prescribed additional fees. If registration is not made within the period specified in that proviso, the company must seek extension of time in accordance with section 87. The Registrar issues a certificate of registration and keeps the prescribed register. A charge is not taken into account by a liquidator or any other creditor unless it is duly registered and a certificate is issued; this does not prejudice the contract or obligation to repay money secured by the charge. Section 78 provides a charge-holder fallback; section 79 applies section 77 to acquisition of property subject to a charge and modifications; section 82 concerns satisfaction. Chapter-default penalties are addressed by section 86. Do not state that non-registration automatically makes the secured debt immediately payable. Legal verification remains open.

sections.heading: Registration duty and deadline
sections.body: A company creating a charge on its property, assets or undertaking, in or outside India, must register the prescribed particulars signed by the company and charge-holder, together with the creating instrument, with the Registrar within thirty days of creation.

sections.heading: Extension for registration
sections.body: On application by the company, the Registrar may allow registration within sixty days of creation on payment of prescribed additional fees. If registration is not made within the period specified in that proviso, the company must seek extension of time in accordance with section 87. Transitional rules for older charges must be checked against the applicable amendment commencement provisions.

sections.heading: Certificate and effect of non-registration
sections.body: The Registrar issues a certificate of registration and maintains the prescribed register. A charge is not taken into account by a liquidator or any other creditor unless duly registered and a certificate is issued. This does not prejudice the contract or obligation to repay the money secured by the charge; non-registration does not, by itself, erase the debt or make it automatically payable.

sections.heading: Related charge provisions
sections.body: Section 78 provides a charge-holder fallback if the company fails to register; section 79 applies section 77 to acquisition of property subject to a charge and modifications; section 82 concerns reporting satisfaction; section 86 addresses chapter-default penalties.

examples.title: Late charge
examples.body: A charge filed after the permitted window does not prevail against the liquidator.

examples.title: Immediate payable
examples.body: The debt itself is not extinguished; it becomes immediately payable.

hypotheticals.question: A company creates a charge and files after thirty days but within sixty days. What should be checked?
hypotheticals.analysis: Section 77 permits the Registrar, on the company's application, to allow registration within sixty days of creation on payment of prescribed additional fees. Check the exact dates, application and prescribed fees.

hypotheticals.question: A charge is not registered. Does section 77 make the secured repayment obligation disappear or automatically become immediately payable?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. The charge is not taken into account by a liquidator or other creditor unless duly registered and certified, but the provision preserves the contract or obligation to repay the money secured. Do not state that non-registration automatically makes the debt immediately payable.

distinctions.title: Charge registration and underlying debt
distinctions.left: Section 77 controls whether a charge is registered and can be taken into account by a liquidator or other creditor.
distinctions.right: The contract or obligation to repay money secured by the charge is not erased by non-registration.

misconceptions.trap: Treating thirty days as the only possible filing period.
misconceptions.correction: The Registrar may allow registration within sixty days of creation on application and prescribed additional fees; beyond that, section 87 extension must be considered.

misconceptions.trap: Assuming non-registration erases the underlying repayment obligation or automatically accelerates the debt.
misconceptions.correction: The section limits whether the charge is taken into account against a liquidator/creditor and expressly preserves the repayment obligation.

misconceptions.trap: Ignoring the creating instrument or signatures required for filing.
misconceptions.correction: The prescribed particulars signed by the company and charge-holder and the instrument creating the charge must be filed in the prescribed form.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Does non-registration wipe out the debt?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: No. The charge is vulnerable against the liquidator and creditors; the secured sum becomes immediately payable.
